h1: Cattreya Place — New 2025 Serviced Apartment on Rim Khlong Prapa Road, Bang Sue Bangkok
intro: As Bang Sue cements its position as Bangkok's newest transit hub, a new crop of practical, affordable accommodation has followed. Cattreya Place is one of the freshest entries — a 3-star serviced apartment that opened in 2025 at 494 Rim Khlong Prapa Phang Kwa Road, in the heart of Bangkok's Bang Sue district. It sits approximately 600 metres (an 8-minute walk) from Tao Poon MRT, the city's only interchange between the Blue and Purple lines, and just ~920 metres from Bangkok Grand Station (Krung Thep Aphiwat) — Thailand's largest railway hub and the future starting point for high-speed rail. Four room types range from 35 to 68 m², all with free parking, free Wi-Fi and a keycard-based self check-in system. Rates start from approximately ฿1,200 per night.

body.html: Bang Sue is not a sightseeing district — it is a logistics district, and one of Bangkok's most powerful. Tao Poon MRT is the only interchange between the Blue and Purple lines, giving guests direct access to Silom, Sukhumvit and Chatuchak in under 30 minutes, or a seamless transfer north into Nonthaburi via the Purple line. Bangkok Grand Station (Krung Thep Aphiwat), Thailand's largest rail terminus with direct overnight trains to Chiang Mai, Khon Kaen and beyond, is a 12-minute walk from the front door. For travellers passing through Bangkok rather than lingering in it, Cattreya Place is precisely what the neighbourhood needed in 2025: a clean, spacious, well-priced base.

The property offers four room configurations, each notably generous in floor area for this price bracket. The Deluxe King Room (35 m², Floor 2) is the entry option, well-sized for a couple. The Comfy Queen Room (63 m², Floor 3) and Family Room (65 m², Floor 2) offer substantial space for families or those wanting room to spread out. The 1 Bedroom + Living Room (68 m², Floor 4) adds a separate lounge area — a rarity at this price level in Bang Sue. All rooms include air-conditioning, refrigerator, free Wi-Fi and a keycard self check-in system, which is particularly convenient for late arrivals or early departures.

"The room was much larger than I expected at this price. The A/C was powerful, the bed comfortable, and there were more power outlets than I've ever seen in a Thai hotel. Free parking sealed the deal."

Trip.com's early reviewers — nine guests as of mid-2025, reflecting the hotel's brand-new status — give the property an overall score of 7.2 out of 10, with Facilities scoring highest at 7.8. The recurring praise centres on three things: room size, air-conditioning strength and the unusually high number of power outlets, which digital travellers find genuinely useful. Free parking, uncommon for budget accommodation in inner Bangkok, also features prominently in positive comments. The self check-in system is praised by those who arrive outside standard reception hours — a practical advantage for rail travellers on unpredictable schedules.

Honest context is necessary too. A few reviewers flag that the bathroom can feel small relative to the generous bedroom footprint, particularly in the Deluxe King configuration. The building entrance is not immediately obvious from the street — saving a Google Maps pin before arrival is strongly advised. As a hotel that opened in 2025, Cattreya Place is still building its review volume; consistency over longer periods has not yet been fully demonstrated. There is no restaurant or breakfast service on site, though the Rim Khlong Prapa corridor has local eateries and the Gateway Bang Sue mall is roughly a kilometre away.

The neighbourhood context adds practical value. Tao Poon MRT (600 m) connects to the Blue line's full circle — Chatuchak, Silom, Hua Lamphong — and to the Purple line's Nonthaburi extension. Bangkok Grand Station (~920 m) handles long-distance rail to Northern and Northeastern Thailand, plus the Red Line to Don Mueang Airport. The Tao Poon weekend market and various canal-side eateries on Rim Khlong Prapa Road fill the dining gap without difficulty. This is a neighbourhood built for moving through Bangkok efficiently, and Cattreya Place sits at its centre.

The bottom line: Cattreya Place is a promising new property still earning its reviews. Its core pitch — unusually spacious rooms, free parking, flexible self check-in and a competitive price starting around ฿1,200 — is well-suited to the transit traveller who values practicality over amenities. The bathroom size and absence of dining are the two honest trade-offs to factor in. If you need a solid base near Bangkok Grand Station without paying hotel-corridor prices, this is a genuinely good option in 2025.

honestSummary: Cattreya Place is a new property still building its track record, but its core strengths are clear: unusually spacious rooms, free parking, keycard self check-in, and rates from around ฿1,200. The honest trade-offs are a smaller bathroom in some room types and no on-site dining. For transit travellers needing a practical, well-sized base near Bangkok Grand Station, this is a solid 2025 choice.
honestChecks: If a large bathroom matters to you — consider the Comfy Queen (63 m²) or 1 Bedroom Suite (68 m²) over the Deluxe King (35 m²); the entry room's bathroom feels tight relative to the price.
If you need breakfast or on-site dining — this hotel has neither. The Rim Khlong Prapa corridor has local Thai food stalls and Gateway Bang Sue mall is about 1 km away.

If you are transiting through Bangkok Grand Station or commuting via MRT — Cattreya Place is an excellent choice: spacious rooms, free parking, keycard check-in and an 8-minute walk to Tao Poon interchange.

tips.title: Save Google Maps Before You Arrive
tips.body: The building entrance is not immediately obvious from the street. Search 'Cattreya Place Bangkok' on Google Maps before leaving MRT Tao Poon Exit 3 and walk ~600 m along Rim Khlong Prapa Phang Kwa Road. Having the navigation ready saves considerable confusion on a first visit.

tips.title: Understand the Self Check-in Process
tips.body: Cattreya Place uses a keycard self check-in system — genuinely useful for late arrivals or early departures. Read the confirmation email or SMS instructions before arriving so the check-in process is smooth on the day.

tips.title: Breakfast? Head to Rim Khlong Prapa
tips.body: No breakfast is provided on site. The Rim Khlong Prapa canal road has local Thai food stalls, coffee shops and convenience stores within walking distance. The Tao Poon morning market (~800 m) is worth the short walk for a proper local breakfast.

tips.title: Travelling with Pets? You Are Welcome Here
tips.body: Cattreya Place accepts dogs and cats at ฿300 per pet per night — one of the very few pet-friendly budget properties in Bang Sue. Plan ahead: confirm the policy when booking as terms can change at new properties.

faqTitle: FAQ — Cattreya Place Bang Sue Bangkok

faq.q: Where exactly is Cattreya Place and how close is it to the MRT?
faq.a: Cattreya Place is at 494 Rim Khlong Prapa Phang Kwa Road, Bang Sue, Bangkok 10800. It is approximately 600 metres from Tao Poon MRT — the only interchange between Bangkok's Blue and Purple lines — a walk of around 8 minutes. Bangkok Grand Station (Krung Thep Aphiwat) is ~920 metres away, about 12 minutes on foot.

faq.q: How much does Cattreya Place cost per night?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿1,200 per night for the Deluxe King Room (35 m²). The Comfy Queen (63 m²) starts at around ฿1,204; the Family Room (65 m²) and 1 Bedroom + Living Room (68 m²) are priced higher. Always check live rates on Trip.com or Booking.com before booking as prices fluctuate with demand.

Yes — free parking is available at the property. This is genuinely uncommon for budget serviced apartments in inner Bangkok and makes Cattreya Place a practical choice for guests arriving by private car.

faq.q: Are pets allowed at Cattreya Place?
faq.a: Yes. Cattreya Place accepts dogs and cats at a charge of ฿300 per pet per night. It is one of the few pet-friendly budget properties in the Bang Sue neighbourhood — confirm the current policy when booking.

faq.q: How do I get from Cattreya Place to Bangkok Grand Station or Don Mueang Airport?
faq.a: Bangkok Grand Station (Krung Thep Aphiwat) is ~920 m — walk south along Rim Khlong Prapa Road for about 12 minutes. It serves long-distance trains to Northern and Northeastern Thailand plus the Red Line to Don Mueang Airport. Don Mueang is ~15.8 km from the hotel; allow around 30 minutes by taxi or ride-share.
